title: Crispy Buttermilk Chicken Sandwich
summary: Buttermilk-marinated chicken thighs get a double-textured, deeply crunchy crust and a quick fry, then stack into a sandwich with spicy mayo, crisp lettuce and pickles.
equipment: large bowl and a shallow dish
heavy, deep pot or casserole (about 24 cm, at least 10 cm deep)
digital probe thermometer (for oil and chicken)
wire rack set over a baking tray

ingredients.note: about 600 g total, trimmed of excess fat

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Whisk the buttermilk with the salt, garlic powder, paprika and cayenne, then add the chicken and turn to coat. Covered and refrigerated for at least 1 hour, or up to 24 hours, the chicken has time to brine: salt helps the meat hold onto its moisture, while the mild acid in the buttermilk softens the surface so the coating has something to grip.

steps.title: Build the dredge
steps.text: Whisk the flour, cornflour, baking powder, salt, paprika and pepper together in a shallow dish. Drizzle in 2 tablespoons of the marinade and rub it through with your fingertips until small shaggy clumps form — these turn into extra-crunchy bits once fried. The cornflour gives a crisper, less greasy crust, and the baking powder adds tiny bubbles that lighten it.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Pour oil into the heavy pot to a depth of about 5 cm, keeping it no more than half full so there is room for bubbling. Heat over medium-high until the thermometer reads 175°C; this usually takes 10-15 minutes. Set a wire rack over a tray ready for draining.

steps.title: Coat the chicken
steps.text: Lift each thigh from the marinade, letting the excess drip off, then press it firmly into the flour mixture on both sides, packing the coating on well. Rest the coated pieces on a rack for 10 minutes so the coating hydrates slightly — this short rest stops it falling off the moment the chicken hits the oil.

steps.title: Fry in batches
steps.text: Two pieces at a time go into the oil, lowered away from you. The temperature will dip to around 150-160°C; adjust the heat to hold it between 150-165°C. Fry for 6-8 minutes, turning once halfway, until deep golden brown and the thickest part reads 74°C — thighs stay juicy even a little above this.

steps.title: Drain and rest
steps.text: The wire rack, not kitchen paper, is where the chicken should land, since kitchen paper traps steam underneath and softens the crust. Sprinkle with a pinch of salt if you like, and let the oil climb back to 175°C before frying the next batch.

steps.title: Build the sandwich
steps.text: Stir the mayonnaise with the lemon juice and cayenne to make the spicy mayo. Spread it over the toasted buns, then layer on the lettuce, the fried chicken and the pickle slices, and serve immediately while the crust is at its crispest.

tips: Keep an eye on the thermometer: oil that's too cool gives a greasy, pale crust, and oil that's too hot browns the outside before the inside is cooked.
Fry only 2 pieces at a time — overcrowding drops the oil temperature and the chicken won't crisp properly.
Leave each piece alone for the first minute of frying so the crust has time to set before you move it.
Let the oil cool completely before straining and storing it; it can be reused once or twice, but never leave hot oil unattended, and keep a lid nearby in case it ever catches.
If the oil ever smokes heavily, turn off the heat; if it catches fire, cover with a lid or damp tea towel and never use water.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: This sandwich is best enjoyed fresh and crisp. Cooked chicken keeps in the fridge for 2 days; reheat on a rack in the oven at 200°C (180°C fan) for 10-12 minutes until piping hot (74°C) and crisp again. Don't freeze the raw chicken while it's still in its buttermilk marinade. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
